title: PaymentRecorded
description: The canonical record of a payment state transition on any Baalvion property. Every site emits this and nothing else — it is what makes one admin panel able to show every payment across the estate, attributed to a site and a tenant. Money is carried as an integer count of minor units in a string, never a JSON number, so no consumer can parse it into a float.

paymentId.description: Canonical payment id — stable across every transition of this payment.

siteId.description: Which property took the money. Resolved from @baalvion/sites; never inferred from a host at consume time.

tenantId.description: Who within the property earned it — an Amarisé store, a paid community, a law firm. Null only where the site itself is the earner.

partyId.description: The group-wide customer id. Null until the party graph is backfilled; never a per-site customer id.

customer.description: Who paid, as the producing site knows them — the signal the party graph resolves a group-wide identity from. Carries only what identity resolution needs; `emailVerified` and `phoneVerified` matter because an unverified value is a string someone typed and must never merge two people.

authUserId.description: The platform account, when the customer was signed in. The strongest identity signal available.

emailVerified.description: Whether the address was proven (a confirmed link, an OAuth provider, a verified login) — not merely entered.

name.description: Display and review only. Never a match key.

siteCustomerId.description: The producing site's own id for this customer.

state.description: The canonical lifecycle state from @baalvion/payment-consistency. There is no sixth state and no service-local variant.

provider.description: The PSP that handled it (razorpay, stripe, payu, cashfree, crypto, bank).

rail.description: The payment rail, which must be one the site is granted in @baalvion/sites.

providerPaymentId.description: The PSP's own id for this payment, for reconciliation against their settlement report.

amount.description: Integer count of minor units as a string — paise, cents, or whole yen. A string so a 64-bit value survives JSON.

exponent.description: Digits after the decimal point for this currency: 2 for INR, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD.

fee.description: What the processor kept. Null when the provider has not reported it yet — a fee that is unknown must not be recorded as zero, or every margin figure derived from it is overstated.

amount.description: Integer count of minor units as a string — paise, cents, or whole yen. A string so a 64-bit value survives JSON.

exponent.description: Digits after the decimal point for this currency: 2 for INR, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD.

net.description: money minus fee — what the business actually received. Null while the fee is unknown, for the same reason.

amount.description: Integer count of minor units as a string — paise, cents, or whole yen. A string so a 64-bit value survives JSON.

exponent.description: Digits after the decimal point for this currency: 2 for INR, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD.

idempotencyKey.description: Stable key for this transition. A consumer that sees it twice must apply it once.

orderRef.description: The producing site's own reference (order id, subscription id, community slug) for support and dispute handling.

failureReason.description: Set only when state is FAILED. Never echoes a raw provider message.
